novel_features.name: New-since per saved search
novel_features.description: See which Uber postings appeared in or closed from a saved search since its last complete scan
novel_features.rationale: Diffs each saved search's baseline id set against the local posting history and advances only after a complete uncapped sync, which no Uber endpoint offers
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on a recurring check of a market so an agent reports only what changed instead of re-listing everything. Create the name with save first (an unknown name exits 3); the first run only takes the baseline; when the careers site refuses, saved searches with a keyword are not diffed, and ones with a work pattern exit 7 (or, in auto mode, use the last local sync)

novel_features.name: Tracker liveness check
novel_features.description: Report whether each known posting id is still open, closed, never seen or unknown, with the date it closed
novel_features.rationale: Answers from complete-scan history kept in the local store, and reports a refused scan as unknown rather than closed
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to keep tracker rows honest in one call instead of one lookup per id

novel_features.name: Disqualifier screen with evidence
novel_features.description: Keep or drop postings by phrases in their description and show the sentence each phrase matched
novel_features.rationale: Runs full-text matching over HTML-stripped descriptions in the local store, which the careers site cannot filter on
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to rule out postings that need sponsorship, relocation or a language, with the evidence sentence an agent can quote. The match is literal, so read the sentence (--verdict all) to judge negations. Check meta.source: under the Oracle fallback descriptions are null, every posting is unscreened and the default --verdict keep is empty. In auto mode it reads the last local sync whatever its age (meta.note gives the date)

novel_features.name: Hiring stats with churn
novel_features.description: Count open, newly posted, opened and closed Uber postings per country, team, subteam or category
novel_features.rationale: Joins postings, every location of multi-location postings, and first-seen and closed-on history in the local store
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for a market read-out of where Uber is hiring and how fast roles turn over; opened_30d and closed_30d stay null until the local store's first complete sync is 30 days old, and are always null on a live read. In auto mode it counts from the last local sync whatever its age (meta.note gives the date)

novel_features.name: Tracker-ready postings feed
novel_features.description: List Uber postings for an ISO3 market, newest first, in the single envelope a job tracker parses
novel_features.rationale: Maps ISO3 codes to the site's country names, reads the whole corpus in one fresh page and sorts by the true posting date, which the site's relevance order does not
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this as the default read for any market pull; it keeps the tracker's flags and field names stable

novel_features.name: Get one posting by id
novel_features.description: Fetch one Uber posting by its id and exit not-found when the site no longer lists it
novel_features.rationale: Asserts that the returned id equals the requested one instead of trusting the first search hit
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent has one id and needs the full posting or a reliable gone signal

novel_features.name: Filter values from the site
novel_features.description: List the countries, teams, subteams, contract types and work patterns the careers site currently offers
novel_features.rationale: Reads the facet lists the site embeds in its job list page, the only source of exact filter values and of the ISO3 map
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before filtering so team and country values match the site exactly

novel_features.name: Save a named search
novel_features.description: Store a named set of filters so new can diff it on every later run
novel_features.rationale: Keeps saved searches in the local store, so a typo in new exits not-found instead of silently starting a fresh baseline
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this once per recurring market check before running new

novel_features.name: List and delete saved searches
novel_features.description: Show every saved search with its filters, baseline size and last advance, or delete one by name
novel_features.rationale: Reads the saved-search tables in the local store, which no Uber endpoint holds
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to audit what new will diff, or to prune stale searches

narrative.headline: Every public Uber job posting as one tracker-ready JSON feed with offline history, new-since diffs and a fallback when the careers site refuses
narrative.value_prop: Pull open Uber postings by country, team or keyword into the single envelope a job tracker already parses, keep a local history of what opened and closed, and screen descriptions for sponsorship or language disqualifiers with the matching sentence shown. When the careers site refuses a request, reads fall back to Uber's own Oracle candidate-experience API instead of returning nothing. That fallback has limits: description and job_category are null; --team, --sub-team, --contract-type, --work-pattern and the description filters have no fallback (the command exits 7 instead); neither do facets or the raw careers commands; and new does not diff saved searches that use a keyword.
narrative.auth_narrative: No account and no key are needed because the CLI reads public postings only and never signs in, applies or subscribes to alerts

quickstart.comment: Confirm the binary runs, without touching the network
The newest postings in one market, in the tracker's envelope
Mirror every open posting locally so history and offline commands work
Name a search once so new can diff it on every later run
See what appeared or closed in that search since its last complete scan (the first run takes the baseline)
Where Uber is hiring right now, with churn once history builds up

troubleshoots.symptom: Exit code 7 with a careers-site refusal message
troubleshoots.fix: Neither the careers site nor the Oracle fallback answered; the error text says which refused. Nothing more is sent to that host until 00:00 UTC, so rerun after then, or use --data-source local to read the last sync

troubleshoots.symptom: The DNS or transport exit code from any command
troubleshoots.fix: Check your resolver or VPN split DNS, then run uber-jobs-pp-cli doctor

Read that row's note for the cause. Run uber-jobs-pp-cli sync --json only when it names a missing or stale local sync; after a refusal, wait until 00:00 UTC, since a fallback sync never counts as a complete one

troubleshoots.symptom: A posting looks missing right after it went live
troubleshoots.fix: Search replies are edge-cached for hours; new and check tolerate the lag, so rerun after the cache refreshes

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs Uber's public job postings as structured data, such as building a shortlist for a market, keeping a job tracker's Uber rows current, or reporting where Uber is hiring. It never writes to Uber: sync, save, searches --delete and new write only the CLI's local store. Run sync on a schedule to build the history that check, stats and screen read offline, so repeated checks report only what changed.
anti_triggers: Applying to an Uber job or filling in an application form
Subscribing to Uber job alerts or managing a candidate profile
Job postings at any employer other than Uber
Uber rides, Uber Eats or any other Uber product API
